In June 2025, Halden Group made a lead commitment to Meridian Capital Partners V, a EUR 1.2 billion fund targeting lower-mid-market buyouts in European industrial technology and business services.

Halden Group was attracted to Meridian on the strength of a track record that is, in our view, genuinely exceptional.

It has realised a gross MOIC of 2.4 times across 17 exits, placing it in the top quartile of European lower-mid-market managers.

The team's stability, with no senior departures across the last three fund cycles, suggests key-person risk may be limited.

Fund IV is currently marked at 1.9 times gross MOIC and a 24% gross IRR.

Meridian Capital Partners V is a EUR 1.2 billion fund targeting lower-mid-market buyouts in European industrial technology and business services.

The fund will hold investments for four to six years and will not deploy more than 30% of commitments outside the EU.

On balance, Halden Group believes the fund should deliver returns broadly in line with its predecessor and recommends the commitment.

The GP provided access to co-investments that would not otherwise have been available to Halden Group.

Halden Group expects the relationship to deepen over the life of the fund.

In June 2026, Partners Group committed to Meridian Capital Partners V, a EUR 1.2 billion flagship fund from Meridian Capital targeting lower-mid-market buyouts in European industrial technology and business services companies.

The fund intends to build a portfolio of 10-14 control-oriented investments, with equity checks of EUR 80-100 million apiece.

Target companies are expected to have enterprise valuations in the range of EUR 20-100 million, annual EBITDA of EUR 5-25 million, and defensible positions in niche industrial or B2B markets.

Partners Group was attracted to this investment given Meridian Capital's strong track record on its prior vintage funds, coupled with its well-established investment team and operational approach to value creation.

Furthermore, Partners Group has a long-established relationship with the manager, having invested alongside Meridian Capital on several co-investments and debt financings, while also making several secondary investments in its earlier funds.

This relationship enabled deep insight during the diligence phase.
